mainEntity.name: How do I calculate sales tax?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiply the pre-tax price by the combined sales tax rate as a decimal. For example, $1,250 at 9.5% is $1,250 × 0.095 = $118.75 in tax, for a total of $1,368.75.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove sales tax from a total?

acceptedAnswer.text: Divide the tax-inclusive total by (1 + rate). A $1,368.75 total at 9.5% tax is $1,368.75 ÷ 1.095 = $1,250 before tax, so the tax was $118.75.

mainEntity.name: Which states have no sales tax?

acceptedAnswer.text: Delaware, Montana, New Hampshire and Oregon have no statewide or local general sales tax. Alaska has no state sales tax, but many Alaskan localities charge their own.
